title: TypeScript in Frontend Applications knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a typed frontend still validate?
options: Only CSS class names need types.
User input and server responses at runtime, while keeping loading, success and failure states explicit.
Nothing: JSX and TypeScript guarantee every browser value is valid.
The frontend can decide server authorization by itself.
questions.answer_key: User input and server responses at runtime, while keeping loading, success and failure states explicit.
questions.explanation: Typed UI models improve development feedback but do not replace runtime validation or server-side checks.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “TypeScript in Frontend Applications”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with integrating with a frontend build tool and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with integrating with a frontend build tool and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Integrating with a frontend build tool”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “TypeScript in Frontend Applications”?
options: Assume separating type checking and application bundling is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check organizing browser code, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check organizing browser code, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Organizing browser code”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
